title: Finger Strength Test - One Arm
texts:  Finger Strength Test – One Arm Assessment Test
Single Arm Finger Strength Testing Session

This testing session is designed to assess finger strength using a single-arm dead hang protocol. 

You should use this session before and after several weeks or months of training to measure the effectiveness of your training. Results from this session also provide an excellent baseline from which to calculate the intensities of other sessions, such as max hangs. 

Complete this session after at least 24 hours of rest from any other climbing or training. Remember to warm up thoroughly before starting this session and warm up your fingers specifically for the hold size, grip position, and body position. 

Complete up to 8 sets of progressively harder hangs until you reach a maximal score. Each hang must follow the rules below:

-  Hang from one arm
-  Complete each hang using a strict half crimp position or a 4 finger open grip position
-  Each hang must be 10 seconds long
-  Your arm should be in a position from 90-180 degrees
-  Only test if you’re able to keep your shoulder in an engaged position throughout 
-  At the completion of the first rep, rest 30 sec and then repeat the test with the other arm

A max score is the highest load completed for the set time staying in the same grip position throughout. Once the load is too high for you to maintain either the grip or arm position, put your feet on the ground immediately and record your scores. 

Most climbers will need to use a pulley and weight set up to make loading sub-bodyweight. For example, if you weigh 70kg and your personal maximum is 60kg of force on a single-arm, you would need a 10kg assistance set up. 

Recording your score:

Maximal total loading (1RM) = Bodyweight +/- added weight or assistance
Maximal body weight % = (Total load / body weight) x 100 

For example: 

60kg (total load) = 70kg (body weight) – 10kg (weight on assistance pulley)
85.7% (body weight %) = (60kg total load / 70kg body weight) x100

Safety guidance:

Any maximal testing session includes some form of risk. Please follow the rules below to reduce the risk of injury and always seek advice from a professional coach if you are unsure of how to perform this testing safely. 

-  Do not change grip positions whilst hanging. If your fingers move or open out whilst hanging, you should stop immediately and place your feet on the ground. 
-  Load your fingers cautiously and progressively when building up to your maximum during testing. 
-  Increase the load of each set progressively, never exceeding an adjustment of more than 5kg on any set. Typically adjustments of 1-2kg are normal. 
-  If you have not reached a max load within 8 sets, finish testing and complete this session on another day. 

Note:
The testing duration was increased from 5s to 10s to correspond with the typical training duration used in one-arm max hang workouts.
